Don't use multiple ad block programs. They likely have overlapping filter lists, so it's pointless (and if anything they may end up fighting one another, but citation needed on that one).

It's possible you have a virus on your computer if you're getting a lot of popups. In any case, I'd recommend one of the following:

In AdBlock Plus, open up the settings and uncheck the box for "allow non-intrusive ads". What AdBlock defines as non-intrusive is still pretty annoying. Either that, or uninstall both the adblockers you have now and simply install uBlock.

If you suspect that your computer has viruses, I'd recommend scanning the computer with SuperAntiSpyware and Malwarebytes. If you have any other problems you can always PM me for help.

In AdBlock Plus, open up the settings and uncheck the box for "allow non-intrusive ads". What AdBlock defines as non-intrusive is still pretty annoying.

Plus it allows reddit ads. That got it unchecked the other day.
Ghostery is pretty great for blocking trackers, something to think about installing too.

Noscript is probably the most thorough choice, since most ads don't run without javascript (and are often hosted by other sites than the one you're browsing).

It will take you a little while to whitelist all the sites you visit regularly, but it's great for enhancing your web-browsing security as well. Harder to get infected by anything if the scripting and redirects on naughty sites are disabled by default.

The users all mentioning NOSCRIPT (for Firefox - not sure about Chrome and IE / Spartan) know it.

NoScript the best. Just remember not to "temporarily allow" anything if you don't know what it is ...
By far the best, been running it for a few years now and since then I have not had a single instance of malware on my computer. Pages load quicker, too.

If you're visiting US-centric websites, scan for viruses, because you have one. If you're not, find a more European/Asian specific blocklist depending on where you're from. I still get ads on a couple of Russian and Japanese websites even though I'm using uBlock Origin.

Regardless, you should install uBlock Origin because it's better.
